questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -ão usually take -ões: limão, limões. The same pattern gives lição, lições.
The word agrees with the person speaking, not the person thanked. A woman says obrigada, a man says obrigado.
Chamar-se is reflexive: literally 'I call myself Ana'. European Portuguese attaches the pronoun after the verb, chamo-me.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Eu ____ de Faro.' (I am from Faro)
questions.explanation: Origin is permanent identity, so it takes ser: sou de Faro. Estar would describe a temporary state or a location right now.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Eles ____ em Lisboa esta semana.' (They are in Lisbon this week)
questions.explanation: Where someone is takes estar: estão em Lisboa. Ser would claim Lisbon is what they permanently are.
quinze = 15. Do not confuse it with cinco (5) or cinquenta (50).
Porto carries the article o, and de plus o contracts to do. A city with a feminine article would give da, as in da Figueira.
Mãe is feminine, so both the article and the possessive agree: a minha mãe. European Portuguese keeps the article before the possessive.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Nós ____ português em casa.' (We speak Portuguese at home)
questions.explanation: Regular -AR verbs take -amos for nós: falamos. Falam is eles, falas is tu, falo is eu.
Onde asks about place. Quando asks when, quem asks who, como asks how.
